lesson_title: Squares, Cubes and Roots of Integers and Rational Numbers
hook_text: Two thirds of two thirds of a pizza. Draw it.
clip_script:
Here is a fraction squared that you can see. A pizza is cut into three equal strips and you take two of them: two thirds of the pizza. Now someone says: take two thirds of what you have. Two thirds of two thirds. Cut your two strips crossways into three and take two of those three rows. You now have a two-by-two block of small pieces out of a three-by-three grid of the whole pizza: four pieces out of nine. Two thirds squared is four ninths.

The picture explains the rule. Squaring the numerator counts the small pieces you have — two rows of two, four. Squaring the denominator counts the small pieces in the whole — three rows of three, nine. Top squared over bottom squared. And it explains why the answer is smaller than two thirds: taking a fraction of a fraction leaves you with less than you started with.
visual_style: A square pizza cut into three strips, two shaded; then cut crossways into a 3-by-3 grid with a 2-by-2 block highlighted; 4/9 appearing
pacing: two cuts, a pause on the grid
call_to_action: Open the full session to handle powers and roots of any fraction or decimal.
